messages.content: Predict a person’s observed allocation in an incentivized investment task. There are two teams, each with four members. Choose amounts for all displayed options at once from a 10-chip endowment. Each amount must be nonnegative and no greater than 10; all four amounts, including keep, must sum exactly to 10. Decimal choices are preserved rather than rounded to integers. option_1 is Pool A: every chip invested gives 0.5 chips to each of the four own-team members, including oneself; it leaves the other team unchanged. option_2 is Pool B: every chip gives 0.5 to each own-team member, including oneself, and subtracts 0.25 from each of the four other-team members. option_3 is Pool C: every chip gives 0.4 to each of all eight people, including oneself. A chip assigned to keep gives one chip only to oneself. These are returns per contributed chip; the invested chip is taken from the 10-chip budget and is not additionally retained. The question states whether the others also choose and can affect the player’s outcomes or cannot affect them. In the mutual case, own-team A/B contributions and everyone’s C can add returns, while other-team B subtracts returns. Other people’s choices are not supplied before the prediction. The local instructions state that one chip is worth £0.50. The final choice screen says one out of twenty participants receives an additional bonus according to decisions; this is separate from participation remuneration. Random selection and payoff calculation occur later. Each person makes this allocation once. Use no current payoff, later questionnaire answers or unannounced later task information. Output only a JSON object with numeric option_1, option_2, option_3 and keep, summing to 10.

Predict a person’s observed allocation in an incentivized investment task. The person chooses amounts for all displayed options at once, using an endowment of 10 chips; amounts must be nonnegative, no greater than 10, and sum exactly to 10 including chips kept. Decimal choices are preserved rather than rounded to integers. Keeping a chip yields one chip only for oneself. The local instructions state that one chip is worth £0.50, separately from participation remuneration. The final choice screen says one out of twenty participants will receive a bonus based on their choices. Selection, matching and payment calculation take place later. For a present-oriented allocation, there are two teams of four, including oneself in the own team: option_1 (Pool A) gives 0.5 chips to each own-team member, including oneself, per chip invested, with no effect on the other team; option_2 (Pool B) gives the same own-team benefit and subtracts 0.25 chips from each of the four other-team members; option_3 (Pool C) gives 0.4 chips to each of all eight people, including oneself. The question specifies whether others can also make choices affecting the current player or whether only the current player makes an allocation. Under mutual influence, other people’s own-team A/B contributions and anyone’s C contributions can benefit the current player, while other-team B contributions reduce the current player’s outcome. Those other decisions are not supplied. For a future-oriented allocation, the final choice descriptions instead direct contributions to three future own-team members and four future other-team members about one year later. They describe no return of contributed chips to the current contributor: the current contributor keeps only the chips assigned to keep. A weak pool gives each future own-team member 0.5 chips per chip contributed and leaves the other team unchanged; a strong pool gives each future own-team member 0.5 and subtracts 0.25 from each future other-team member; a universal pool gives 0.4 to each of all seven future beneficiaries. The question specifies which pools are available. All amounts in the answer are invested or kept chips, never final payoffs. Use only the current task and any explicitly supplied earlier personal allocation. Do not infer a personality type from that earlier action, and do not use later survey answers or current outcomes. Output only a JSON object with the keys specified in the question and numeric amounts summing to 10.

The person chooses amounts for all displayed options at once, using an endowment of 10 chips; amounts must be nonnegative, no greater than 10, and sum exactly to 10 including chips kept. Decimal choices are preserved rather than rounded to integers. Keeping a chip yields one chip only for oneself. For a present-oriented allocation, there are two teams of four, including oneself in the own team: option_1 (Pool A) gives 0.5 chips to each own-team member, including oneself, per chip invested, with no effect on the other team; option_2 (Pool B) gives the same own-team benefit and subtracts 0.25 chips from each of the four other-team members; option_3 (Pool C) gives 0.4 chips to each of all eight people, including oneself. Those other decisions are not supplied. For a future-oriented allocation, the final choice descriptions instead direct contributions to three future own-team members and four future other-team members about one year later. They describe no return of contributed chips to the current contributor: the current contributor keeps only the chips assigned to keep. A weak pool gives each future own-team member 0.5 chips per chip contributed and leaves the other team unchanged; a strong pool gives each future own-team member 0.5 and subtracts 0.25 from each future other-team member; a universal pool gives 0.4 to each of all seven future beneficiaries. The question specifies which pools are available. All amounts in the answer are invested or kept chips, never final payoffs. Use only the current task and any explicitly supplied earlier personal allocation. Do not infer a personality type from that earlier action, and do not use later survey answers or current outcomes. Output only a JSON object with the keys specified in the question and numeric amounts summing to 10.

The person chooses amounts for all displayed options at once, using an endowment of 10 chips; amounts must be nonnegative, no greater than 10, and sum exactly to 10 including chips kept. Decimal choices are preserved rather than rounded to integers. Keeping a chip yields one chip only for oneself. For a present-oriented allocation, there are two teams of four, including oneself in the own team: option_1 (Pool A) gives 0.5 chips to each own-team member, including oneself, per chip invested, with no effect on the other team; option_2 (Pool B) gives the same own-team benefit and subtracts 0.25 chips from each of the four other-team members; option_3 (Pool C) gives 0.4 chips to each of all eight people, including oneself. Those other decisions are not supplied. For a future-oriented allocation, the final choice descriptions instead direct contributions to three future own-team members and four future other-team members about one year later. They describe no return of contributed chips to the current contributor: the current contributor keeps only the chips assigned to keep. A weak pool gives each future own-team member 0.5 chips per chip contributed and leaves the other team unchanged; a strong pool gives each future own-team member 0.5 and subtracts 0.25 from each future other-team member; a universal pool gives 0.4 to each of all seven future beneficiaries. The question specifies which pools are available. All amounts in the answer are invested or kept chips, never final payoffs. Use only the current task and any explicitly supplied earlier personal allocation. Do not infer a personality type from that earlier action, and do not use later survey answers or current outcomes. Output only a JSON object with the keys specified in the question and numeric amounts summing to 10.

Decimal choices are preserved rather than rounded to integers. Keeping a chip yields one chip only for oneself. The local instructions state that one chip is worth £0.50, separately from participation remuneration. The final choice screen says one out of twenty participants will receive a bonus based on their choices. Selection, matching and payment calculation take place later. For a present-oriented allocation, there are two teams of four, including oneself in the own team: option_1 (Pool A) gives 0.5 chips to each own-team member, including oneself, per chip invested, with no effect on the other team; option_2 (Pool B) gives the same own-team benefit and subtracts 0.25 chips from each of the four other-team members; option_3 (Pool C) gives 0.4 chips to each of all eight people, including oneself. The question specifies whether others can also make choices affecting the current player or whether only the current player makes an allocation. Under mutual influence, other people’s own-team A/B contributions and anyone’s C contributions can benefit the current player, while other-team B contributions reduce the current player’s outcome. Those other decisions are not supplied. For a future-oriented allocation, the final choice descriptions instead direct contributions to three future own-team members and four future other-team members about one year later. They describe no return of contributed chips to the current contributor: the current contributor keeps only the chips assigned to keep. A weak pool gives each future own-team member 0.5 chips per chip contributed and leaves the other team unchanged; a strong pool gives each future own-team member 0.5 and subtracts 0.25 from each future other-team member; a universal pool gives 0.4 to each of all seven future beneficiaries. The question specifies which pools are available. All amounts in the answer are invested or kept chips, never final payoffs. Use only the current task and any explicitly supplied earlier personal allocation. Do not infer a personality type from that earlier action, and do not use later survey answers or current outcomes. Output only a JSON object with the keys specified in the question and numeric amounts summing to 10.

The person chooses amounts for all displayed options at once, using an endowment of 10 chips; amounts must be nonnegative, no greater than 10, and sum exactly to 10 including chips kept. Decimal choices are preserved rather than rounded to integers. Keeping a chip yields one chip only for oneself. The local instructions state that one chip is worth £0.50, separately from participation remuneration. The final choice screen says one out of twenty participants will receive a bonus based on their choices. Selection, matching and payment calculation take place later. For a present-oriented allocation, there are two teams of four, including oneself in the own team: option_1 (Pool A) gives 0.5 chips to each own-team member, including oneself, per chip invested, with no effect on the other team; option_2 (Pool B) gives the same own-team benefit and subtracts 0.25 chips from each of the four other-team members; option_3 (Pool C) gives 0.4 chips to each of all eight people, including oneself. The question specifies whether others can also make choices affecting the current player or whether only the current player makes an allocation. Under mutual influence, other people’s own-team A/B contributions and anyone’s C contributions can benefit the current player, while other-team B contributions reduce the current player’s outcome. Those other decisions are not supplied. For a future-oriented allocation, the final choice descriptions instead direct contributions to three future own-team members and four future other-team members about one year later. They describe no return of contributed chips to the current contributor: the current contributor keeps only the chips assigned to keep. A weak pool gives each future own-team member 0.5 chips per chip contributed and leaves the other team unchanged; a strong pool gives each future own-team member 0.5 and subtracts 0.25 from each future other-team member; a universal pool gives 0.4 to each of all seven future beneficiaries. The question specifies which pools are available. All amounts in the answer are invested or kept chips, never final payoffs. Use only the current task and any explicitly supplied earlier personal allocation. Do not infer a personality type from that earlier action, and do not use later survey answers or current outcomes. Output only a JSON object with the keys specified in the question and numeric amounts summing to 10.

The person chooses amounts for all displayed options at once, using an endowment of 10 chips; amounts must be nonnegative, no greater than 10, and sum exactly to 10 including chips kept. Decimal choices are preserved rather than rounded to integers. Keeping a chip yields one chip only for oneself. The local instructions state that one chip is worth £0.50, separately from participation remuneration. The final choice screen says one out of twenty participants will receive a bonus based on their choices. Selection, matching and payment calculation take place later. For a present-oriented allocation, there are two teams of four, including oneself in the own team: option_1 (Pool A) gives 0.5 chips to each own-team member, including oneself, per chip invested, with no effect on the other team; option_2 (Pool B) gives the same own-team benefit and subtracts 0.25 chips from each of the four other-team members; option_3 (Pool C) gives 0.4 chips to each of all eight people, including oneself. The question specifies whether others can also make choices affecting the current player or whether only the current player makes an allocation. Under mutual influence, other people’s own-team A/B contributions and anyone’s C contributions can benefit the current player, while other-team B contributions reduce the current player’s outcome. Those other decisions are not supplied. For a future-oriented allocation, the final choice descriptions instead direct contributions to three future own-team members and four future other-team members about one year later. They describe no return of contributed chips to the current contributor: the current contributor keeps only the chips assigned to keep. A weak pool gives each future own-team member 0.5 chips per chip contributed and leaves the other team unchanged; a strong pool gives each future own-team member 0.5 and subtracts 0.25 from each future other-team member; a universal pool gives 0.4 to each of all seven future beneficiaries. The question specifies which pools are available. All amounts in the answer are invested or kept chips, never final payoffs. Use only the current task and any explicitly supplied earlier personal allocation. Do not infer a personality type from that earlier action, and do not use later survey answers or current outcomes. Output only a JSON object with the keys specified in the question and numeric amounts summing to 10.

Random selection and payoff calculation occur later. Each person makes this allocation once. Use no current payoff, later questionnaire answers or unannounced later task information. Decimal choices are preserved rather than rounded to integers. option_1 is Pool A: every chip invested gives 0.5 chips to each of the four own-team members, including oneself; it leaves the other team unchanged. option_2 is Pool B: every chip gives 0.5 to each own-team member, including oneself, and subtracts 0.25 from each of the four other-team members. option_3 is Pool C: every chip gives 0.4 to each of all eight people, including oneself. A chip assigned to keep gives one chip only to oneself. These are returns per contributed chip; the invested chip is taken from the 10-chip budget and is not additionally retained. The question states whether the others also choose and can affect the player’s outcomes or cannot affect them. In the mutual case, own-team A/B contributions and everyone’s C can add returns, while other-team B subtracts returns. Other people’s choices are not supplied before the prediction. The local instructions state that one chip is worth £0.50. The final choice screen says one out of twenty participants receives an additional bonus according to decisions; this is separate from participation remuneration. Random selection and payoff calculation occur later. Each person makes this allocation once. Use no current payoff, later questionnaire answers or unannounced later task information. Output only a JSON object with numeric option_1, option_2, option_3 and keep, summing to 10.
